title: Carboxylic Acid Derivatives
description: Recognize acyl families and reason through addition–elimination mechanisms.
objectives: Identify esters, amides, anhydrides, lactones, and lactams

sources.label: Supplied Kaplan curriculum: Chapter 9; section scope checked against local body and summary

review.note: Original explanations and exercises; source-backed author review, not independent expert verification.

lessons.label: Recognize acid derivatives
lessons.title: Recognize acid derivatives
lessons.tag: Read the atom directly attached to acyl carbon

cards.rule: Esters have C(=O)–OR; amides have C(=O)–NR2; anhydrides have C(=O)–O–C(=O). Lactones are cyclic esters and lactams are cyclic amides. A beta-lactam contains a four-membered ring.
cards.cue: Acyl C → O–C: ester. Acyl C → N: amide. Acyl C → O → acyl C: anhydride.
cards.trap: An ether has no adjacent carbonyl. An N-substituted amide is still an amide even if it has no N–H bond. Ring size names count heteroatoms as ring members.
cards.app: Triacylglycerols contain ester links; proteins contain amide links. Beta-lactam antibiotics exploit a strained amide structure.

steps.label: 1. Ester vs. amide
steps.text: Ethyl propanoate connects the acyl carbon to oxygen. The alkoxy carbon chain lies beyond that oxygen.

steps.label: 2. Cyclic amide
steps.text: The beta-lactam has four ring atoms, one of them N. The carbonyl carbon is part of the ring and the oxygen is outside it.

steps.label: 3. Cyclic ester
steps.text: A lactone contains an ester linkage within a ring. This five-membered lactone has one ring oxygen and four ring carbons.

cards.rule: A nucleophile adds to an acyl carbon and shifts the pi pair to O. Collapse of the tetrahedral intermediate reforms C=O and expels a leaving group. For comparable unactivated derivatives, a useful order is acid chloride > anhydride > ester > amide. Leaving-group basicity and resonance donation both matter.
cards.cue: Addition–elimination replaces the acyl substituent while retaining a carbonyl.
cards.trap: Aldehydes and ketones usually undergo addition because H− or an ordinary carbanion would be poor leaving groups. Acid/base catalysis and ring strain can change rates. Conjugation does not universally increase carbonyl electrophilicity.
cards.app: Amide resonance makes peptide bonds relatively resistant to uncatalyzed hydrolysis. Strained beta-lactams are more reactive than ordinary unstrained amides.

steps.label: 1. Add to the carbonyl
steps.text: Hydroxide attacks the ester carbonyl carbon while the pi pair moves to oxygen. The arrow shows that pi-pair movement, not the entire mechanism.

steps.label: 2. Tetrahedral intermediate
steps.text: The carbon now bears the incoming OH, the original OCH3, and an O− derived from the carbonyl oxygen. It has four single bonds.

steps.label: 3. Collapse
steps.text: An oxygen lone pair reforms C=O, and the C–OCH3 bond pair moves to the leaving oxygen. Subsequent proton transfer yields carboxylate plus methanol under basic conditions.

cards.rule: Anhydrides react with water to give acids, with alcohols to give ester plus acid, and with amines to give amide plus acid-derived products. Transesterification exchanges one OR group for another under suitable catalysis. Acidic amide hydrolysis gives carboxylic acid and protonated amine; basic hydrolysis gives carboxylate and amine.
cards.cue: Follow the acyl fragment and the departing group separately.
cards.trap: In basic ester hydrolysis, carboxylate formation helps drive the net reaction. Do not draw a free carboxylic acid as the major product until acid workup. Amide hydrolysis usually needs more forcing conditions than ester hydrolysis.
cards.app: Proteases catalyze peptide hydrolysis under mild biological conditions by activating nucleophiles and stabilizing intermediates; the uncatalyzed reaction is much slower.

steps.label: 1. Anhydride cleavage
steps.text: Water attack at either equivalent acyl carbon of ethanoic anhydride leads overall to two ethanoic acid molecules.

steps.label: 2. Exchange an ester group
steps.text: In transesterification, the O-alkyl group can be replaced by the incoming alcohol-derived group while the acyl carbon skeleton remains.

steps.label: 3. Hydrolyze an amide
steps.text: An amide’s N donation lowers electrophilicity and its leaving group is poor unless conditions enable departure. Strong acid/base with heating or a catalyst can accomplish hydrolysis.

stages.prompt: Select the ring nitrogen and carbonyl carbon.
stages.explanation: A–B is the amide C–N linkage in the ring.
hints: Find N bonded directly to C=O carbon.
Select both endpoints of that bond.

stages.prompt: How many atoms are in the ring?
stages.explanation: The ring contains N plus three carbons; the carbonyl oxygen is exocyclic.
hints: Do not count the oxygen outside the ring.

stages.explanation: A cyclic amide is a lactam.
hints: Use the heteroatom attached to the acyl carbon.

exercises.summary: A beta-lactam is a four-membered cyclic amide.

exercises.label: Follow addition–elimination
exercises.title: Follow addition–elimination

stages.prompt: After addition, what restores the carbonyl?
options: Collapse of a tetrahedral intermediate with leaving-group departure
Loss of the methyl carbon as methane
stages.explanation: The oxygen lone pair reforms C=O as a leaving group departs.
hints: The acyl carbon must return to three sigma directions.
Reform the pi bond and expel the heteroatom leaving group.

stages.prompt: Among comparable ordinary anhydrides, esters, and amides, which is least reactive toward acyl substitution?
stages.explanation: Amides have strong N-to-carbonyl resonance donation and a poor leaving group.
hints: Consider lone-pair donation and leaving-group basicity.
Nitrogen strongly stabilizes the amide system.

exercises.summary: Acyl substitution proceeds by addition and elimination.

stages.prompt: Select the O-bound methyl carbon that leaves with the alkoxy fragment.
hints: Distinguish the acyl methyl from the O-methyl.
Follow the single-bonded oxygen away from the carbonyl.

stages.prompt: Under excess aqueous NaOH, the major acid-derived product is…
stages.explanation: The product is deprotonated under strongly basic conditions.
hints: Account for acid–base chemistry after substitution.
Carboxylic acids have much lower pKa than water.

stages.prompt: What alcohol is produced from the O-methyl group?
stages.explanation: The departing methoxide is protonated to methanol.
hints: Replace its bond to acyl carbon with H on oxygen.
